title: Empirical mathematics in Australian Indigenous Smoke Telegraphy
summary: Mathematics curriculums at most universities tend to perpetuate a belief that higher mathematics is historically and culturally European. First Nations and minority students may not see their identities and cultures reflected in the discipline, yet university mathematics educators are keen to diversify and broaden the appeal of their courses. This article presents an investigation on the mathematics of smoke telegraphy, as a contribution to inlaying cross-cultural mathematical heritage in the curriculum.
